source: ACGME Laboratory Genetics and Genomics Milestones 2.0

level_1: Describes the importance of clinical history for optimal test selection
Recommends the optimal test option(s) based on clinical or family history, with assistance
Independently suggests modifications to existing laboratory workflows based on clinical need
level_2: Identifies elements of a laboratory test request
Evaluates a specimen for pre-analytic errors, with assistance
Creates an algorithm for test selection based on clinical history
level_3: Gathers pertinent elements of the clinical history to aid in test selection
Suggests modifications to existing laboratory workflows based on clinical need, with assistance
Creates a new protocol to assist the laboratory in the appraisal of specimen issues
level_4: Recognizes sources of pre-analytic error
Independently recommends the optimal test(s) based on clinical or family history
Independently develops a new laboratory workflow
level_5: Describes rationale behind existing routine laboratory workflows
Independently evaluates a specimen for pre-analytic errors and identifies possible resolutions

level_1: Describes basic principles for major assays performed in the laboratory
Explains possible sources of QC failures
level_2: Describes quality control (QC) in the clinical laboratory
Independently performs assays
level_3: Performs assays, with substantial assistance
Investigates QC failures and proposes resolution
level_4: Identifies QC failures
Develops new, alternate, or improved assay
level_5: Performs assays, with minimal assistance
Identifies and implements a new QC approach for a clinical test

level_1: Identifies normal results
Integrates results with the clinical history to develop a final interpretation, with assistance
level_2: Discusses the importance of patient’s clinical history to test interpretation
Independently interprets results
level_3: Interprets simple results, with assistance
Independently integrates results with the clinical history to develop a final interpretation
level_4: Gathers pertinent elements of the clinical history to aid in interpretation
Develops an improved result interpretation workflow
level_5: Interprets complex results, with assistance
Identifies novel correlations between results and clinical history

level_1: Identifies the elements of a laboratory report
Drafts a revised report, with assistance
level_2: Identifies that reports can be revised
Independently generates concise reports for complex cases
level_3: Drafts a report for simple cases using accurate terminology/ nomenclature, with assistance
Independently generates a revised report
level_4: Identifies when to correct, amend, or addend a report based on the type of alteration required
Develops a new reporting template for original or revised reports
level_5: Drafts a report for complex cases using accurate terminology/ nomenclature, with assistance

subcompetencies.name: Foundations of Medical Genetics and Genomics

level_1: Defines relevant medical terminology
Recognizes the pathogenic mechanisms for well-described conditions
Independently correlates genomic alterations and phenotypic information to guide laboratory testing and interpretation
level_2: Explains basic structure and function of the genome
With assistance, assimilates and integrates medical information to generate a differential diagnosis
Independently applies understanding of pathogenic mechanisms to interpretation of test results
level_3: Describes the basic mechanisms of germline and somatic disease development
Correlates genomic alterations and phenotypic information to guide laboratory testing and interpretation, with assistance
Mentors others in the process of integration of clinical and laboratory findings to generate a differential diagnosis
level_4: Describes genetic conditions using accurate medical terminology
Applies understanding of pathogenic mechanisms to interpretation of test results, with assistance
Presents a new clinical genomic/phenotypic correlation
level_5: Identifies the basic genomic alterations underpinning abnormal lab results
Independently assimilates and integrates medical information to generate a differential diagnosis

level_1: Defines the basic components of a test validation and verification
Determines the optimal technologies and platforms for genetic tests, with assistance
level_2: Describes various methodologies used in a clinical genetics laboratory
Independently calculates test performance characteristics
level_3: Describes methods and data used in establishing test performance characteristics for validation and verification
Independently determines the optimal technologies and platforms for genetic tests
level_4: Describes the strengths and limitations of a genetic laboratory test
Designs a test validation/verification and establishes QC metrics
level_5: Determines test performance characteristics, with assistance
Independently designs a new test for a genetic condition

level_1: Describes common patient safety events
Describes laboratory QI initiatives
Conducts analysis of patient safety events and offers error prevention strategies (simulated or actual)
Develops and assesses
level_2: Identifies that processes exist for reporting patient safety events
Participates in analysis of patient safety events (simulated or actual)
Reports patient safety events (simulated or actual event)
QI initiatives at the institutional or community level
level_3: Demonstrates knowledge of QI concepts
Given a safety-related concern, can describe the risk management process of disclosing such events to the appropriate individuals
Demonstrates the skills required to identify, develop, implement, and analyze a QI project
level_4: Identifies system factors that lead to patient safety events
Participates in laboratory
Actively engages teams and processes to modify systems to prevent patient safety events
level_5: Defines the institutional process of safety reporting systems
QI initiatives
Develops innovative protocols to detect and report safety events

level_1: Identifies the importance of coordinating care
Performs safe and effective transitions of care/hand-offs
level_2: Explains the importance of effective transitions of care and hand-offs
Coordinates care with the clinical and laboratory team
level_3: Describes effective care coordination with the clinical and laboratory team
Models and advocates for safe and effective transitions of care/hand- offs
level_4: Describes examples of safe and effective transitions of care/hand- offs
Improves quality of transitions of care within and across health care delivery systems to optimize patient outcomes
level_5: Coordinates care with the clinical and laboratory team, with assistance

subcompetencies.name: Laboratory Geneticist’s Role in Health Care System

level_1: Identifies key components of the health care system
Collaborates with the other members of the health care system, with assistance
Independently drafts the assessment of a laboratory fiscal metric for director review
level_2: Identifies basic types of medical reimbursement
Identifies opportunities for cost-effective patient care
Advocates for or leads systems change that enhances high-value, efficient, and effective patient care
level_3: Describes how components of a health care system are interrelated, and how this impacts patient care
Identifies inter- relationship between fiscal responsibility and quality metrics in a lab (e.g., balancing staffing needs, test reagent needs, cost containment, and billing efficiency)
Participates in a local or national committee related to fiscal issues in genetic testing
level_4: Identifies testing documentation related to billing and reimbursement
Independently collaborates with the other members of the health care system
level_5: Describes the financial components related to the laboratory operation
Practices cost-effective patient care

level_1: Identifies laboratory accreditation and licensing agencies
Independently evaluates quality indicators, including proficiency testing results
level_2: Defines terminology related to laboratory quality
Actively participates in the laboratory self- inspection
level_3: Describes the accreditation process, its requirements and necessary documentation
Formulates a response for a proficiency test failure (actual or simulated)
level_4: Interprets quality data and charts and trends, including proficiency testing results, with assistance
Participates in the inspection of an external laboratory
level_5: Participates in review of laboratory practice to assure compliance with accreditation requirements
Reviews the quality management plan to identify areas for improvements

level_1: Demonstrates familiarity with basic technical concepts of hardware, operating systems, databases, and software for general purpose applications
Independently uses resources to perform routine variant classification using professional standards and guidelines
level_2: Identifies the various resources including software, tools and databases used for classification of variants
Applies informatics tools as needed in laboratory initiatives (e.g., data management and security, computational statistics, information governance)
level_3: Identifies laboratory specific software, key technical concepts, interfaces, workflow, barcode application, and automation systems (enterprise systems architecture)
Independently uses resources to reclassify ambiguous variants
level_4: Uses resources to classify variants in the context of the phenotype, with assistance
Proposes medical informatics improvements for the operation of the laboratory
level_5: Discusses laboratory initiatives based on informatics (system implementation and configuration)
Contributes to the knowledge base for the refinement of ambiguous test results and variant classifications

level_1: Demonstrates how to access and select applicable evidence
level_2: Identifies and applies the best available evidence and/or clinical laboratory standards/guidelines to guide diagnostic evaluation of simple cases
level_3: Identifies and applies the best available evidence and/or clinical laboratory standards/guidelines to guide diagnostic evaluation of complex cases
level_4: Critically appraises and applies evidence to guide lab-based recommendations, even in the face of conflicting data
level_5: Mentors others to critically appraise and apply evidence for complex cases; and/or participates in the development of laboratory standards/guidelines

subcompetencies.name: Reflective Practice and Commitment to Personal Growth

level_1: Realizes responsibility for personal and professional development by establishing goals
Designs and implements a learning plan, with assistance
Critically evaluates the effectiveness of behavioral changes in narrowing the gap(s) between expectations and actual performance
level_2: Identifies the gap(s) between expectations and actual performance
Seeks performance data and feedback with respect
Uses performance data to measure the effectiveness of the learning plan and improves it when necessary
level_3: Actively seeks opportunities to improve
Institutes behavioral change(s) to narrow the gap(s) between expectations and actual performance
Coaches others in personal and professional development
level_4: Demonstrates willingness to receiving performance data and feedback in order to inform goals
Independently creates and implements a learning plan
Facilitates the design and implementation of learning plans for others
level_5: Analyzes and reflects on the factors which contribute to gap(s) between expectations and actual performance
Models appropriate and thoughtful seeking and consideration of feedback

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of the ethical principles underlying laboratory testing
Demonstrates professional behavior in complex or stressful situations
level_2: Describes how to report professionalism lapses, including strategies for addressing common barriers
Manages complex ethical situations
level_3: Analyzes straightforward situations using ethical principles
Recognizes situations that may trigger professionalism lapses and intervenes to prevent lapses in self and others
level_4: Demonstrates insight into professional behavior in routine situations; takes responsibility for own professionalism lapses
Identifies and seeks to address system-level factors that introduce or exacerbate ethical problems or impede their resolution
level_5: Recognizes the need for and uses appropriate resources to seek solutions in managing and resolving complex ethical situations
Coaches others when their behavior fails to meet professional expectations

level_1: Responds promptly to instructions, requests, or reminders to complete tasks and responsibilities
level_2: Takes ownership and performs tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner
level_3: Anticipates situations that may impact own ability to meet responsibilities and describes the impact on team
level_4: Shares responsibility for system outcomes as a member of the team
level_5: Designs new strategies to ensure that the needs of patients, teams, and systems are met

level_1: Describes common indicators of personal or professional well-being
level_2: Independently recognizes status of personal and professional well-being and seeks help when needed
level_3: Proposes a plan to optimize personal and professional well-being
level_4: Implements a plan to optimize personal and professional well-being
level_5: Coaches others to develop and implement plans to optimize personal and professional well- being

level_1: Identifies common barriers to effective communication
Uses nonverbal behavior to demonstrate respect and establish rapport while observing a complex result disclosure by a clinician
level_2: Identifies the role of the laboratory in communicating results to patients
Communicates the content of a report or educational materials in a way that is accessible to patients and families
level_3: Identifies complex barriers to effective communication
Orally communicates simple results to families in a concise manner, under the supervision of an attending clinician
level_4: Uses nonverbal behavior to demonstrate respect and establish rapport while observing in the clinical setting and can identify factors that could make a clinical situation psychosocially complex
Develops systems to communicate laboratory information in a way that is accessible to patients and families
level_5: With prompting, reflects on biases and can identify barriers in written language that may challenge understanding by patients and families
Independently orally communicates laboratory results with relevant information to providers

level_1: Uses language that values all members of the health care team, including clinical and laboratory professionals
Integrates feedback from team members to improve own communication and other skills
level_2: Describes the utility of constructive feedback
Independently communicates information effectively with all health care team members, including clinical and laboratory professionals
level_3: Adapts communication style to fit team needs
Facilitates regular health care team-based communications and feedback in complex situations
level_4: Solicits feedback on personal performance as a member of the laboratory team
Models flexible communication strategies that value input from all health care team members, resolving conflict when needed
level_5: Communicates information effectively with all health care team members, including clinical and laboratory professionals, with assistance

level_1: Protects patient personal health information by following institutional policies
Uses institutional structure to effectively communicate clear and constructive suggestions
level_2: Identifies institutional and departmental procedures for communication of issues
Independently communicates clinical information
level_3: Selects content, recipient, and communication methods based on context and clinical urgency, with guidance
Initiates conversations on difficult subjects with appropriate stakeholders to improve the system
level_4: Uses institutional structure to effectively communicate clear and constructive suggestions, with assistance
Models effective communication of clinical information
level_5: Effectively and securely communicates clinical information, with guidance
Facilitates dialogue regarding systems issues among larger community stakeholders
